candidates.name: Link/idle-aware backlight auto-dim
candidates.user_value: Readable by day, glare-free at night; a dead USB link is visible as a dimmed panel from across the room.
candidates.implementation_cost: 40 lines of pure logic plus one GUI call; no new pins, tasks, or drivers (GPIO6 PWM already owned by core BSP).
candidates.risk: Low: wrong brightness at worst; core meter path never branches on it; active-low polarity per vendor BSP fact.
candidates.verification_method: Host C test of production file (normal/dim thresholds, link loss, activity restore) plus operator unplug-and-watch procedure.
candidates.selection_reason: Only candidate using an already proven actuator with no new failure surface and full host verifiability.

candidates.name: IMU tilt page-turn
candidates.user_value: Flip screens by tilting the board when it sits behind a monitor.
candidates.implementation_cost: New I2C BSP plus sensor driver port and gesture tuning, about 300 lines.
candidates.risk: Medium-high: new I2C boot-path failure surface and accidental flips from desk vibration disturb the core reading task.
candidates.verification_method: Host tilt-classifier unit test plus operator tilt-left/right/idle procedure (planned, not built).
candidates.selection_reason: Highest integration risk; deferred until the core USB-to-LCD path is observed passing on hardware.

candidates.name: RTC-backed last-good clock
candidates.user_value: Wall-clock last-good time and true source-age on the status screen.
candidates.implementation_cost: I2C BSP plus time-base arbitration and a clock-invalid UI state, about 200 lines.
candidates.risk: Medium: backup-cell presence is unconfirmed, so the clock could show confidently wrong times, violating the unknown-until-determined rule.
candidates.verification_method: RTC present/absent host matrix plus operator power-cycle retention check (planned, not built).
candidates.selection_reason: Depends on the unconfirmed backup-power fact; an unreliable clock is worse than the honest unknown display.
